title: Minimum Adjacent Swaps to Group All 1s in a Circular Binary Array
statement: Given a circular binary array nums (where the last element is adjacent to the first), return the minimum number of adjacent swaps required to group all 1s together in any contiguous block. A swap exchanges two adjacent elements. The array is circular, meaning the first and last elements are considered adjacent.
summary: Find the minimum adjacent swaps needed to group all 1s in a circular binary array.

examples.explanation: There are 5 ones. The optimal window of size 5 with maximum ones is [1,1,0,0,1] (indices 4-0 circularly) which has 3 ones, requiring 2 swaps to bring the two outside ones in. Alternatively, window [1,0,1,1,1] (indices 6,7,0,1,2) has 3 ones, also requiring 2 swaps.
Only one 1, so no swaps needed.
Three 1s. Best window of size 3 has two 1s (e.g. [1,0,1]), so one zero inside needs to be swapped out, requiring one swap.
